questions.question: What is Brownian motion?
options: The random motion of particles suspended in a medium.
The settling of large solid particles at the bottom of a liquid.
The chemical reaction between a solute and a solvent.
The process of a liquid turning into a gas at its boiling point.

questions.question: How does increasing the temperature affect the movement of particles in a gas or solution?
options: They slow down and eventually stop moving.
They move more quickly.
They clump together and form a solid.
Their movement is completely unaffected by temperature.

questions.question: Why is a suspension not classified as a solution?
options: Because its components can never be separated.
Because the particles are too small to be seen and never settle.
Because solid particles can be seen in it and will eventually settle over time.
Because it always contains only one single pure substance.

questions.question: What must happen to the forces of attraction between solute particles for a substance to dissolve?
options: They must be strengthened.
They must remain completely unchanged.
They must be overcome.
They must convert into chemical bonds.

questions.question: What can happen to the total volume of a mixture when two different liquids are mixed together?
options: It is always exactly equal to the sum of the individual volumes.
It can be less than expected because one type of particle fits into the spaces between another.
It always doubles because particles push each other further apart.
It increases because new particles are created during mixing.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding dissolving and melting?
options: Dissolving and melting are identical processes.
Dissolving is a chemical change, while melting is a physical change.
Dissolving is not the same as melting, but both are physical processes.
Dissolving requires a chemical reaction, whereas melting does not.

questions.question: What is formed when a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent?
options: A suspension
A solution
A new element
A precipitate

questions.question: If 10 g of salt is dissolved in 100 g of water, what is the total mass of the resulting mixture?
What piece of equipment and unit would you typically use to measure the volume of a liquid in a school laboratory?
options: A balance, measured in grams
A thermometer, measured in degrees Celsius
A measuring cylinder, measured in cm³
A ruler, measured in centimeters

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a pure material?
options: It melts and boils over a wide range of temperatures.
It has a fixed melting point and boiling point.
It cannot be heated to its boiling point without decomposing.
Its melting point changes every time it is measured.

questions.question: What effect do impurities have on the melting and boiling point of a material?
options: They have no effect whatsoever.
They make the melting and boiling point completely disappear.
They change the melting and boiling point of the material.
They always make the melting point exactly equal to the boiling point.

questions.question: How do the melting and boiling behaviors of mixtures compare to those of pure substances?
options: Mixtures melt or boil over a range of temperatures.
Mixtures melt and boil at one exact, fixed temperature.
Mixtures do not have any melting or boiling points.
Mixtures only boil and can never be melted.

questions.question: At a given temperature, what limit exists when dissolving a solute in a solvent?
options: There is no limit to how much solute can dissolve.
Only a maximum of 1 gram can ever be dissolved.
There is a limit to how much solute can dissolve in a solvent.
Solutes can only dissolve if the solvent is constantly boiling.

questions.question: What might happen to the dissolved solute as a hot, saturated solution cools down?
options: The solute will turn into a gas and escape.
The solute may become insoluble and start to crystallize out.
The solute will permanently chemically bond with the solvent.
The volume of the solvent will suddenly double.

questions.question: Which of the following factors can affect the solubility of a substance?
options: Only the color of the container used.
The size of the solute pieces, the choice of solvent, or the temperature of the solvent.
Only the atmospheric pressure in the room.
The shape of the laboratory bench.
